channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Australian Dollar reverses as Iran risks lift USD ahead of Fed minutes
item.description: The Aussie Dollar reversed its course against the Greenback on Tuesday as investors remain uncertain of the outcome of the Middle East conflict, which tends to push energy prices higher, increasing the likelihood that major central banks would need to tighten monetary policy.

item.title: Trump, Carney hold last-minute talks ahead of new 50% tariffs on Canadian goods
item.description: US President Donald Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney are negotiating in an effort to reach an agreement on tariffs, with just hours to go before the United States (US) imposes 50% tariffs on hockey sticks, wine and an array of other Canadian imports, CNBC reported on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold steadies below $4,350 as surging yields offset support from Fed rate-hold bets
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) holds steady near $4,335 after pulling back from an early-June top near $4,450 during the early Asian trading hours on Wednesday. The precious metal faced some selling pressure in the previous session as Treasury yields surged to their highest levels in decades.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: SMAs confluence blocks bulls near 185.00
item.description: The EUR/JPY registers two consecutive days of gains, but on Tuesday, buyers failed to gain traction as they faced a confluence of key resistance levels near the 184.70 area. The cross-pair is poised to end the day unchanged, near its opening price of 184.69.

item.title: The Japanese Yen gives back half a record intervention
item.description: The Dollar trades near 159.50 against the Yen on Tuesday after a session high just short of 160.00, the strongest level the pair has reached since Tokyo and Washington intervened together at the end of July.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Bulls stall near 216.00 as RSI flattens
item.description: The GBP/JPY consolidates at familiar levels on Tuesday, virtually unchanged near 216.00, with the cross-pair seesawing within the 215.85-216.22 range, as neither buyers nor sellers are able to clear key resistance/support levels during the day.

item.title: British Pound Sterling's three-month high was made in America
item.description: The British Pound trades just short of 1.3550 against the Dollar on Tuesday, holding inside Monday's range after a peak short of 1.3600 carried it to its strongest level since early May. That leaves close to 300 pips of recovery from the base just short of 1.3300 built in the first week of August.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar holds steady amid a firm US Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD hovers around the 0.5870 zone at the time of writing on Tuesday, marginally lower on the day. The pair is treading water as a firm US Dollar (USD) and a cautious market mood keep the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) on the back foot.

item.title: US President Trump says no Iran talks; naval blockade remains
item.description: The US President Donald Trump posted on his social network that “there are no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled, with the Islamic Republic of Iran. The Naval Blockade remains in full force and effect. The Hormuz Strait is open and operating.

item.title: Mexican Peso dips on Middle East tensions, eyes on FOMC minutes
item.description: The Mexican Peso loses some ground on Tuesday, depreciating by about 0.16% against the US Dollar as investors await the release of the Federal Reserve’s last meeting minutes, with a resolution of the US-Iran conflict remaining unlikely.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Sideways range holds against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) analysts Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/CNH has been trading quietly, with intraday ranges clustered around current levels.

item.title: South Korean Won: Bearish Won view with 1,400 support – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities turns bearish on the Korean Won, arguing USD/KRW is likely to find support around 1,400 as prior KRW strength fades.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Flag support rebound keeps bulls alive
item.description: The USD/CHF pair recovers some ground on Tuesday after testing the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) of 0.7866 along with the bottom trendline of the ‘bearish flag’, which so far contained price action amid the lack of conviction of buyers and sellers, regarding the trend’s direction.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar firms on Hormuz jitters ahead of UK CPI and FOMC Minutes
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) held a firm tone near the 99.60s on Tuesday, keeping a mild safe-haven bid as tensions around the Strait of Hormuz stayed front and center. Gold and Oil both sold off, and most major currencies drifted lower against the Greenback.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Upside risk stays in focus against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD rebounded after a sharper-than-expected drop to 1.2752, easing immediate downside pressure and pointing to intraday consolidation between 1.2760 and 1.2795.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Gradual appreciation view – MUFG
item.description: MUFG analysts Lin Li and Khang Sek Lee note that July data point to weaker Chinese growth and a widening divergence between the "new" and "traditional" economy.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Strong exports underpin SGD – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Singapore-focused FX research highlights robust non-oil domestic exports driven by electronics and AI-related demand, with NODX growth already above the government’s upgraded full-year forecast.

item.title: Economists agree: BoE will hold rates through year-end – Reuters poll
item.description: The Bank of England (BoE) will keep interest rates unchanged for the rest of the year, according to a Reuters poll conducted between August 13 and 18.

item.title: Japanese Yen drifts lower as Greenback retains safe-haven bid
item.description: USD/JPY holds modest gains near the 159.60s on Tuesday, edging higher on the day. The pair has clawed back ground after a recent sharp pullback and is grinding back toward the upper end of its recent range.

item.title: Indonesia Rupiah: Fiscal discipline supports stability – UOB
item.description: UOB economist Enrico Tanuwidjaja reviews Indonesia’s 2027 State Budget, highlighting a calibrated balance between growth and fiscal discipline that matters for the Rupiah and local bonds.

item.title: Gold price falls as US yields surge, pressuring bullion
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) retreats on Tuesday as US Treasury yields keep their momentum, while energy prices rise further amid a lack of progress in talks between the US and Iran. XAU/USD trades at $4,364, down over 1.10%.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD consolidates as bullish momentum fades
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) edges lower on Tuesday, remaining confined within a week-old trading range as bullish momentum softens following the recent rally. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $63.96, down 2.77% on the day.

item.title: A two-decade yield high buys the Dollar Index nothing
item.description: The highest long-dated US yields in nearly two decades have moved the US Dollar Index (DXY) by three hundredths of a point.

item.title: The Dow Jones Industrial Average has a term premium problem
item.description: A quarter-point Federal Reserve (Fed) increase by December stopped being a certainty over the past eight days, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average is lower for it.

item.title: Australian Dollar declines from two-month highs as Hormuz tensions lift the US Dollar
item.description: AUD/USD trades just below 0.7100 on Tuesday, a touch lower for the day and sliding from the two-month highs reached on Monday.

item.title: Euro fails to hold gains over the Pound ahead of UK inflation
item.description: EUR/GBP slips toward 0.8550 at the time of writing on Tuesday, with the Euro (EUR) unable to hold onto earlier gains against the Pound Sterling (GBP).

item.title: New Zealand Dollar edges lower on US-Iran tensions as RBNZ hike expectations curb losses
item.description: NZD/USD retreats on Tuesday and trades around 0.5880 at the time of writing, down 0.38% on the day. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains under pressure as mounting geopolitical tensions between the United States (US) and Iran fuel risk aversion and support demand for the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Japanese Yen stays on the back foot despite hawkish BoJ expectations
item.description: USD/JPY extends its sideways movement below the 160.00 psychological mark on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) struggles to gain traction.

item.title: Copper: Booming prices face supply risks – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Barbara Lambrecht highlights that Copper prices on the LME are close to record highs, with an unusually large cash–3‑month spread driven by falling LME stocks and tariff-related pre‑emptive buying in the US.

item.title: Euro: Bullish momentum targets mid-1.17s – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Euro (EUR) is resilient around 1.1576, with Germany’s ZEW survey showing improving expectations and a slow recovery backdrop. Short-term EUR/USD technicals are described as bullish, with strong intraday and daily momentum.
